items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: The only other tenors in town that I knew of... were Paul Besey... and Dyson Jones.

ctx.x: You mean Pettis? Pettis. I'm sorry. Oh, I didn't remember whether you meant Schoble or not.

No, I meant Pettis. Well, he took it in to have it gone over, new springs and pads and things. And the only thing they had to lend him in the interim was a tenor. And, which was not hard for him, being a B-flat instrument. And all our tunes were B-flat, E-flat, A-flat. The only other tenors in town that I knew of, and I'm sure that he knew about, were Paul Besey, who was playing in the movie theaters, and Dyson Jones. And the only reason Jones was of any interest to anybody was because of the people in the band.…

and I'm very certain that Bud heard Pettis. Bud had been playing a violin, you see, by request of his family, and I'm quite certain that Bud was influenced quite heavily by Pettis before he ever heard anybody else. Bud's story is that it was Coleman Hawkins.
